_docs.overview: Planets are generated from a seed. Each seed deterministically picks a biome and applies its parameters with seed-driven noise. Edit values → relaunch → watch terminal for 'Item_PlanetType(seed=...) biome=...' to verify changes.
_docs.biome_selection: The seed picks a biome via (seed % num_biomes). Same seed always picks the same biome. To see a specific biome, change the seed in gameConfig.txt until you get the one you want.

field_reference.surfaceTint: [R, G, B] 0.0-1.0 — Base color of the planet surface. Higher = brighter. Mixed with seed-driven noise (20-60% blend). Examples: [0.8, 0.6, 0.3] = warm yellow desert, [0.3, 0.6, 0.2] = green terran, [0.7, 0.8, 0.9] = blue-white ice, [0.9, 0.2, 0.1] = red lava, [0.5, 0.2, 0.8] = purple gas giant.
field_reference.atmoDensityRange: [min, max] — Controls atmosphere thickness and glow. 0.0 = no atmosphere (sharp edge), 1.0 = Earth-like, 2.0 = very thick (Venus-like haze). Higher values make the planet look hazier and more diffuse.
field_reference.cloudLevel: Single value — Height of the cloud layer relative to surface. Negative = clouds below surface (hidden). 0.0 = surface level. 0.15 = raised clouds visible as bright bands. Higher = more prominent cloud bands.
field_reference.cloudLevelRange: [min, max] — If present, overrides cloudLevel with a random range per-planet. Use this for variety within a biome.
field_reference.oceanLevel: 0.0-1.0 — Fraction of surface covered by water. 0.0 = no ocean (dry land). 0.3 = moderate oceans (Earth-like). 1.0 = fully water world. Currently informational only (shader wiring pending).
field_reference.hasRings: true/false — Whether this biome typically has rings. Gas giants and ice worlds usually have rings. Individual planets still have a small random chance to deviate.
field_reference.ringProbability: 0.0-1.0 — Global fallback ring probability if biome doesn't specify hasRings. 0.6 = 60% of planets have rings.
field_reference.wavelengthBase: [R, G, B] — Controls atmospheric scattering color. Lower values = more scattering (redder horizon). The engine divides 1/wavelength^4, so small changes have big visual effect. [0.66, 0.53, 0.4] = Earth-like blue sky.
field_reference.wavelengthJitter: Single value — Random ± variation applied to each wavelength component. 0.1 = each RGB channel varies by ±0.1. Higher = more color variety between planets of the same biome.
field_reference.desaturationRange: [min, max] — How washed out the surface colors are. 0.0 = fully saturated (vivid colors), 1.0 = fully grey. 0.4-1.0 gives natural-looking variety.
field_reference.atmoTintSaturationRange: [min, max] — How saturated the atmosphere glow color is. 0.5 = somewhat grey atmosphere, 1.0 = vivid colored atmosphere.
field_reference.rotationSpeed: float — How fast the planet spins (radians per frame). 0.0001 = slow, 0.0005 = fast gas giant. Currently informational only (shader wiring pending).
field_reference.scale: int — Planet radius in engine units. 100000 = standard. Larger values = bigger planet visually.
field_reference.oceanLevelPower: float — Power curve applied to random ocean level. Higher = more planets tend toward extremes (very dry or very wet). 1.5 = moderate bias.

tips.remove_all_rings: Set hasRings: false on the biome, or ringProbability: 0.0 in defaults
